audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagreed with the packet. Stored: Skill/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Skill/Skill/Tryndamere/Tryndamere. Packet: Garen/Garen/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Tryndamere. The page's own whys[] match the packet, not the chart — whys[0] 'At level 1 Garen's early Q burst beats a Fury-less Tryndamere', whys[1] 'At level 2 you still out-trade', whys[3] and whys[4] both describe Tryndamere winning while the chart said Skill. Several Tryndamere rows also carried 5/10 ratings, which read as even.
audit.why: Tryndamere at level 1 has no Fury, no Spinning Slash and no crit chance; Garen's Q auto-reset beats him outright for two levels. From level 3 the full kit plus Bloodlust healing takes over and never gives the lane back — which is why this is the only losing matchup in the slice at 48.72% over 2730 games.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Garen, Garen, then Tryndamere for all five remaining stages, with ratings adjusted so the Tryndamere rows no longer read as even. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike said Undying Rage makes the ult 'nearly useless' without giving its cooldown, and used the wrong ability name 'Spinning Slashes' (packet flagged this, distance 2 from Spinning Slash).
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80, so 120s at rank 1 — a real, trackable window rather than a permanent condition. That converts a vague warning into a rule: bait it, then execute afterwards. Demacian Justice at 120s rank 1 trades one-for-one with it.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike restated with the 120s cooldown and the bait-then-execute sequence; ability name corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields describe Mocking Shout as an 'attack-speed slow' (mid) or a plain 'slow' (spikes[2]). Riot's text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' It reduces ATTACK DAMAGE, not attack speed, and the movement slow applies ONLY to enemies with their backs turned. The packet flagged the name as suspect at distance 2. Undying Rage was also listed at a 110-second cooldown; the real value is 120/100/80.
audit.why: This is the decisive positional rule in the matchup and it was inverted. A Garen who disengages from Tryndamere gets slowed and chased down; a Garen who keeps facing him takes no slow at all. Combined with Decisive Strike breaking free of all slows on an 8s cooldown, Tryndamere's kiting pressure is far weaker than the page implied — but only if the player knows to turn and face rather than walk away. The AD reduction is the part that actually applies unconditionally, and it hurts a champion whose damage is physical.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout's real effect and its back-turned condition stated in tldr, spikes[2], mid, mistakes and wants.you[1]; Undying Rage given its true 120s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and the all-in window pointed only at a 110s figure that was wrong.
audit.why: Spinning Slash at 12/11/10/9/8 is his gap-closer and escape; Bloodlust is a flat 12s. Those are the trackable numbers, and committing while Spinning Slash is up only feeds Fury.
audit.corrected: All-in window re-keyed to Spinning Slash's 12s rank-1 cooldown plus a spent Undying Rage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The flagged missing interaction — Bloodlust healing decides extended trades — appeared only as the generic phrase 'his healing' in the itemization block, never tied to the ability.
audit.why: Bloodlust consumes stacked Fury to heal on a flat 12s cooldown, so Grievous Wounds timing is the single itemization decision in this lane.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust named in focus, mid, mistakes and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: Track Tryndamere’s Undying Rage (110s): Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then execute. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 and he cannot die while it runs — hold Demacian Justice until it has fully expired.

edits.before: Commit on Undying Rage’s cooldown, at your level/item spikes, and with jungle setup — bait his answer before you spend yours.
edits.after: Commit while Spinning Slash (12s at rank 1) is down and Undying Rage is spent — otherwise you are only feeding him Fury.

edits.before: Fight without anti-heal. Burst into his active R. Chase his spin into fog. Save the R for moments with names on them.
edits.after: Fighting without Grievous Wounds. Bursting into an active Undying Rage. Turning your back, which arms his W slow.

edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned — face him and it is just an attack-damage cut.

edits.after: After a crit first item his sustained DPS outraces your Perseverance, and Mocking Shout cuts your attack damage whether or not you are facing him.

edits.after: From level 3 on he flips the lane: Spinning Slash closes, Fury crits land, and Bloodlust heals off that Fury, so bring Grievous Wounds — and at 6 Undying Rage removes your kill pressure entirely.

notes: Both packet-flagged names were real errors. 'Spinning Slashes' is Spinning Slash. 'Mocking Shout's attack-speed slow' was wrong twice over: the ability reduces attack DAMAGE, and its movement slow applies only to enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere. That second half is the useful discovery on this page — the standard instinct to disengage is exactly what turns Mocking Shout on, and facing him disarms it. Undying Rage's cooldown was also 10 seconds short of the real 120s at rank 1. This is the only losing matchup in the slice (48.72%), and the chart is now consistent with that.
